title: Log sleep
what: A plain Log sleep form with two groups, Bedtime and Wake up, each with a date and a time chip, and Save at top right.
takeaway: Two labelled rows, bedtime and wake up, are the simplest possible manual entry and suit users with no wearable.

title: Edit sleep session
what: An edit screen that splits the night into In bed, Fell asleep, Woke up and Out of bed, with an inline wheel picker open under Out of bed and a red Delete link.
takeaway: Separating time in bed from time asleep gives sleep latency and lie-in time without asking extra questions.

title: Edit sleep on a timeline
what: A vertical hour timeline with draggable sleep blocks from 11:00p to 3:35a and from 4:18a, a hint to press to add awake time, and a toast saying the energy schedule is updating.
takeaway: Showing the night as a block on a timeline makes a waking in the middle easy to mark, and the toast shows the edit changes something real.

title: How did you feel when you woke up
what: A sheet asking how you felt when you woke up, tied to the night's date and times, with Good, OK, Bad and I don't know as face options and a Mood reporting toggle.
takeaway: Three faces plus an honest I don't know option keeps the wake-up mood question fast and low pressure for older users.

title: How well rested did you feel
what: A slider from Not at all to Very that writes a sentence above it, Today I felt moderately rested, with a short note on why the app asks.
takeaway: Turning the slider value into a plain sentence makes the rating feel like the user's own words rather than a number.

title: How was your sleep last night
what: Four large square buttons numbered 1 to 4 and labelled Awful, Bad, Fair and Good under a single question.
takeaway: Big numbered tiles with word labels are an accessible, one-tap sleep quality scale with no neutral midpoint.

title: Sleep quality tags and hours
what: A daily log with illustrated tiles like Trouble falling asleep, Woke up refreshed and Woke up tired, and a large 4 hour 00 min sleep duration field.
takeaway: Diary questions like trouble falling asleep can be single tap tiles rather than separate questions.

title: What happened last night
what: A bottom sheet over the home screen listing night events such as 50+ dB sleeping noise, Device in bed and Late meal, each with a no, unsure and yes toggle, and a Done button.
takeaway: A short yes or no list of last night's factors captures wind-down behaviour in seconds and could feed the wind-down part of the score.

title: Sleep journal
what: A journal of yes or no questions such as Consumed caffeine, Have any alcoholic drinks and, under Nighttime, Ate food close to bedtime, with a notes box and Save Journal.
takeaway: Grouping habit questions under a Nighttime header is a clear model for a wind-down checklist answered the next morning.

title: Set wake-up and wind-down hours
what: An onboarding step with a large heading and two rows, Wake up 9:00 AM and Wind down 10:00 PM, each with a time chip.
takeaway: Asking for wind-down time instead of bedtime frames the goal as a calm routine to start, not a deadline to hit.

title: What's your ideal sleep schedule
what: A 24 hour clock dial with a moon handle at 10:00 pm and a sun handle at 6:00 am, a heading that says Consistency matters, and a line about gentle reminders.
takeaway: One sentence on why consistency matters, placed on the schedule screen itself, explains the score before the user ever sees it.

title: Set your sleep schedule
what: A setup sheet with Sleep Goal 8 hr, an Every Day schedule card with Bedtime 10:30 PM and Wake up 7:00 AM, an Edit link and Add Schedule.
takeaway: Keeping the hours goal separate from the bedtime and wake card lets a coach set duration while the user picks times that fit their life.

title: Sleep Planner goal
what: A planner showing a suggested 9:20 PM bedtime, a 6:20 AM wake time and 9:00 time in bed, with a sheet to pick Improve my sleep or Reach my sleep need.
takeaway: Working back from a fixed wake time to a suggested bedtime is easier to act on than asking users to choose both.

title: Bedtime reminders
what: Two reminders, a Wind-down reminder at 10:30 PM with a tip to set it 30 minutes before bed and a Bedtime reminder at 11:00 PM, with a time wheel open.
takeaway: Two separate nudges, one to start winding down and one for bed, with the 30 minute advice written inline.

title: My Routine
what: A routine built in stages, Unwind then Sleep then Sunrise alarm, with a Reminder to Rest card at the top and an Add step link under each stage.
takeaway: Laying the night out as ordered stages gives a wind-down routine a shape the user can follow step by step.

title: Waking hours
what: A sheet to set Wake-up time 6:00am and Sleep time 11:00pm, with a note that the new day starts at 4:00am, two hours before wake-up.
takeaway: Defining when a new day starts around the user's wake time avoids a late night log landing on the wrong day.

title: Sleep History empty state
what: An empty Sleep History page saying no Sleep Check-Ins yet with a Start Sleep Check-In button.
takeaway: The empty state is a single clear action, not a blank chart.

title: How did you sleep last night
what: A five face scale on a line with the chosen face enlarged and labelled Good, under a personalised question with the user's name.
takeaway: Quality comes first, before any times, so the user can answer even if they don't remember the clock.

title: How many hours did you sleep
what: A clock dial with moon and sun handles set to 2:50 AM bedtime and 9:45 AM wake up, showing 6h 55m total sleep, with a Skip button.
takeaway: Dragging two handles sets bedtime, wake time and duration in one gesture, and Skip keeps it optional.

title: What made your sleep good
what: Selectable chips grouped under Before Sleep, such as Stress and Breathing Exercises, and During Sleep, such as Fell Asleep Quickly and Light.
takeaway: Splitting factors into before sleep and during sleep matches wind-down versus night disturbances.

title: Check-in complete
what: A results page confirming the first check-in, a 7 day bar chart with one bar and a face, Average Time Asleep 6h 55m and a View History button.
takeaway: The night just logged appears right away on the weekly chart, so the user sees their entry counted.

title: Set a daily reminder
what: After recommended content, a Set a Daily Reminder block asks when to check in, with Morning, Afternoon and Night buttons.
takeaway: Asking for a reminder only after the first check-in is done, with three broad time choices, is low effort.

title: Let's look at last night
what: The check-in opens with a star badge, a Tasks completed bar and a task breakdown such as Digital Hygiene and Sleep Wake Schedule.
takeaway: Starting the morning check-in with what the user did yesterday links the routine to the night's result.

title: How did you sleep last night
what: A glowing orb that changes with a five stop slider, here set to Excellent, with a Next button.
takeaway: A single slider with a word label and a visual that responds makes a rating feel rewarding without any numbers.

title: What helped you sleep
what: Chips grouped under Self-Care, Habits and Environment, with Breathing exercises, Consistent schedule, No social media and Quiet room selected, and a Skip link.
takeaway: Asking what helped, rather than what went wrong, keeps the diary positive and still collects wind-down data.

title: Weekly insights
what: An Insights week view where the Check-In card shows Excellent, a row of day circles with Wednesday filled, and counts of what helped.
takeaway: Day circles across the week show check-in consistency at a glance without a score.

title: Sleep page
what: The Sleep page with a 7 day highlight, a Your Schedule card with bedtime and wake up, and a plus button at top right to add data.
takeaway: The schedule sits on the same page as the data, so the target and the actual night are read together.

title: Add sleep, choose type
what: An add sheet listing In Bed, Asleep, Awake, Core, Deep and REM, with Starts and Ends date and time fields below.
takeaway: Stage options only make sense with a wearable; GoodFlip should offer just in bed or asleep for manual users.

title: Add sleep, times set
what: The same sheet with In Bed ticked, Starts Sep 24 11:00 PM and Ends Sep 25 8:00 AM, and a blue tick button to save.
takeaway: Overnight entry needs the start date to roll back to the previous day by default, which this form shows clearly.

title: Sleep saved
what: The Sleep chart in day view now shows 8 hr time in bed as a bar, with the schedule card below.
takeaway: Returning straight to the chart with the new bar confirms the save without a separate success screen.
